Name: Slot-Machine Fatigue (Juice Overload on High-Frequency UI)
Keywords: overuse, confetti, bounce, fatigue, annoying, slow, too much animation, slot machine
Symptom (What Goes Wrong): Every click spawns particles, bounces 15%, or shakes the screen. Users feel exhausted after 5 minutes of work.
Why Developers Do It: Applying Low-Frequency Hero mechanics (particles, hitstop, heavy bounce) to High-Frequency actions (navigation, filtering, standard clicks).
The Game-Feel Fix: Enforce the Frequency × Intensity Matrix: High-frequency actions get <=160ms subliminal compression (0.97 scale) and zero delay; reserve hitstop and particles strictly for rare Hero Moments.
Code Bad vs Good:
BAD: onClick={() => { confetti(); bounceModal(); }} on every filter tab.
GOOD: High-freq tab uses 160ms FLIP pill glide; confetti reserved only for 'Sprint 100% Complete'.

Name: Misapplied Hitstop (Freeze Frames on Navigation/Inputs)
Keywords: hitstop lag, delay, freeze frame, slow navigation, unresponsive
Symptom (What Goes Wrong): Adding an 80ms pause before opening a menu, switching a tab, or typing makes the application feel laggy and broken.
Why Developers Do It: Misunderstanding Hitstop: in games, hitstop happens ON IMPACT after the swing connects, never when moving the character or opening inventory.
The Game-Feel Fix: Navigation, menus, and inputs must respond in <16ms (0ms delay). Use Hitstop (70-100ms hold) ONLY at the climax of high-stakes commits (Deploy, Publish, Pay, Complete).
Code Bad vs Good:
BAD: setTimeout(() => openDropdown(), 90);
GOOD: openDropdown() at 0ms; use 85ms hitstop only on 'Publish Workflow' button commit.

Name: Swallowed Clicks During Entrance/Exit Animations
Keywords: dropped click, ignored input, pointer-events, closing modal blocks click, input buffer
Symptom (What Goes Wrong): Fast users click a button while a modal is fading out or type immediately after pressing Cmd+K, and their click/keystrokes are ignored.
Why Developers Do It: Leaving pointer-events: auto on closing overlays or waiting for onAnimationEnd before focusing inputs or accepting clicks.
The Game-Feel Fix: Apply pointer-events: none at frame 0 of any exit animation, auto-focus inputs at frame 0 of mount, and buffer user clicks during active transitions.
Code Bad vs Good:
BAD: onAnimationEnd={() => inputRef.current.focus()}
GOOD: Focus synchronously on mount + set pointer-events: none immediately on data-state='closed'.

Name: Zero-Coyote Hover Trap (Instant Menu Collapse)
Keywords: hover menu closes, dropdown closes, diagonal mouse path, tooltip flicker, coyote time
Symptom (What Goes Wrong): Moving the cursor diagonally from a trigger button toward a submenu crosses 2px of outside space and instantly snaps the menu shut.
Why Developers Do It: Binding setOpen(false) directly to onMouseLeave without a grace timer or safe-triangle check.
The Game-Feel Fix: Add a 150ms Coyote Time grace timer on pointerleave that is cancelled if the pointer enters the menu content.
Code Bad vs Good:
BAD: onPointerLeave={() => setOpen(false)}
GOOD: onPointerLeave={() => { timer = setTimeout(() => setOpen(false), 150); }}

Name: Symmetric Enter/Exit Sludge
Keywords: slow close, ease-in-out, symmetric duration, modal close slow
Symptom (What Goes Wrong): Modals and dropdowns take 300ms ease-in-out both to open and to close, making dismissal feel sluggish.
Why Developers Do It: Using a single CSS transition property for both open and closed states.
The Game-Feel Fix: Use Asymmetric Velocity: Enter over 220-260ms with cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1); Exit over 120-150ms with cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 1, 1).
Code Bad vs Good:
BAD: transition: all 300ms ease-in-out;
GOOD: .open { animation: in 240ms cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1); } .closed { animation: out 130ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,1,1); }

Name: Layout-Thrashing Squash & Expansion (Animating Width/Height/Margin)
Keywords: jank, 30fps, layout shift, cls, width, height, top, left, margin, reflow
Symptom (What Goes Wrong): Micro-interactions stutter at 20-30fps on laptops/mobile and cause surrounding text to reflow on every frame.
Why Developers Do It: Animating CSS width, height, padding, margin, or top/left instead of compositor-only properties.
The Game-Feel Fix: Animate ONLY transform (translate3d, scale3d, rotate) and opacity, or use grid-template-rows: 0fr -> 1fr / FLIP for layout transitions.
Code Bad vs Good:
BAD: .card:hover { margin-top: -4px; height: 210px; }
GOOD: .card:hover { transform: translate3d(0, -4px, 0) scale(1.01); }

Name: Horizontal Jitter on Animated Counters
Keywords: number jitter, counter width jump, tabular-nums, odometer, timer
Symptom (What Goes Wrong): As a number counter or timer ticks up, the text and adjacent icons vibrate horizontally because '1' is narrower than '8'.
Why Developers Do It: Using proportional default font glyphs on dynamic numbers.
The Game-Feel Fix: Always apply font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums (Tailwind: tabular-nums) to any animated number, price, timer, or badge count.

Name: Unconditional Spatial Motion (Ignoring prefers-reduced-motion)
Keywords: accessibility, prefers-reduced-motion, vestibular, motion sickness, shake, tilt, particles
Symptom (What Goes Wrong): Users with vestibular disorders experience dizziness from 3D card tilts, error shakes, receding background scales, and particle bursts.
Why Developers Do It: Hardcoding animations without media query or matchMedia checks.
The Game-Feel Fix: Preserve the semantic feedback (instant color flash, checkmark swap, tabular number update, audio/haptic if enabled) while bypassing spatial translation, rotation, shake, and particles when prefers-reduced-motion: reduce matches.
Code Bad vs Good:
BAD: Unconditional element.animate(shakeKeyframes)
GOOD: Check window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches -> fallback to border highlight.
